game.title: Mission Control
game.tagline: Design a real space mission. Every choice has a consequence.

capcom.objective: Director, choose where we go. Each target has its own budget and its own problems.
capcom.orbit: How do we meet the target? Fly past, circle it, or land on it. Each way changes fuel, lifetime and science.
capcom.assembly: Build the spacecraft. Watch the six bars on top: every part changes all of them.
capcom.window: Planets move. Launch when Earth and the target line up and the rocket can carry more.
capcom.launch: All stations report GO. Clear the tower.
capcom.mission: The spacecraft is flying. Watch the log. When something goes wrong, you decide.
capcom.debrief: Mission complete. Here is what worked, what didn't, and why.

onboarding: Director, you have one budget and one rocket ride.
Build a spacecraft, launch it and run the mission.
Six resources limit you: Budget, Mass, Power, Data, Comms and Time.
There is no single right answer. Every choice has a consequence.

budget.label: Budget
budget.explain: Money to build, launch and operate the mission (in millions of dollars). Operations cost money every month.

mass.label: Mass
mass.explain: Spacecraft mass including the fuel needed to brake at the target. It must fit what the rocket can lift.

power.label: Power
power.explain: Electricity used on board vs. electricity produced. Solar panels get weaker far from the Sun.

data.label: Data
data.explain: How much data the instruments collect per day. More data means more science, if you can send it home.

comms.label: Comms
comms.explain: How much data the antenna can send to Earth per day. Data that can't be sent is lost.

time.label: Time
time.explain: How long the spacecraft keeps working, compared with the time the science goal needs.

issues.budgetOver: Over budget by ${over}M. Pick cheaper parts or fewer instruments.
issues.massOver: Too heavy by {over} kg. The {rocket} can send {capacity} kg to {destination}. Choose a bigger rocket or drop parts.
issues.powerDead: Only {available} W at {destination}. The spacecraft needs at least {bus} W just to stay alive. It will freeze.
issues.powerLow: Power short: instruments can run only {uptime}% of the time. Add power or remove an instrument.
issues.solarFar: {destination} gets only {sunlight}% of Earth's sunlight, so your panels give {available} W.
issues.commsLow: Only {share}% of your data can reach Earth. A bigger antenna or fewer data-hungry instruments would help.
issues.timeShort: The spacecraft lasts {months} months, but the goal needs {required}.
issues.lunarNight: Solar landers freeze in the 14-day lunar night. Lifetime: about 2 weeks.
issues.requiredPart: {orbit} needs a {part}. Without it the mission will fail.
issues.orbitInstrument: {part} only works on a lander. On this mission it is dead weight.
issues.noInstruments: No instruments: the spacecraft will fly, but bring back no science.
issues.lostPower: Power at {destination}: {available} W. Below survival level. The spacecraft froze.
issues.lostPowerWhy: Too little power to keep the spacecraft alive. Solar panels lose strength fast far from the Sun.
issues.powerCheck: Arrived at {destination}. Switching from cruise power to science power…

launch.text: Lift-off! The {rocket} has cleared the tower.
Max Q: the moment of strongest air pressure on the rocket. Holding steady.
First stage empty and dropped. Lighter rocket, faster climb.
Second stage in orbit at 7.8 km/s. That is 28,000 km/h.
Upper stage burn complete. Leaving Earth toward {destination}.
Spacecraft separated. {power} online, {powerAvailable} W at Earth.

cruise.text: Cruise: {transfer}. The engine is off: the spacecraft coasts along a curve around the Sun.
Small course correction burn. On target for {destination}.

arrival.text: Signal delay now {delay}. The spacecraft has to act on its own.

operations.text: Science is on. Instruments collect {data} GB/day, {share}% reaches Earth.

end.text: Mission complete after {months} months. Great work, Director.

lost.text: We have lost the spacecraft. Let's find out why.

favorite.title: Right tool for the job
favorite.text: {part}: the right instruments for this goal (×1.5 science).

fullDownlink.title: All data reached Earth
fullDownlink.text: Your antenna sent everything the instruments collected.

lowDownlink.title: Data stuck on board
lowDownlink.text: Only {share}% of your data reached Earth. A high-gain antenna sends 4× more.

lowPower.title: Not enough power
lowPower.text: Instruments ran only {uptime}% of the time because power was short.

shortLife.title: Mission ended early
shortLife.text: The spacecraft worked {months} of the {required} months the goal needed.

longLife.title: Long life
longLife.text: The spacecraft outlived the goal: {months} months of work.

budgetLeft.title: Money left over
budgetLeft.text: ${left}M left. Real agencies use savings to extend missions.

oversized.title: Rocket too big
oversized.text: You used only {use}% of the rocket's capacity. A smaller rocket would save ${save}M.

deadWeight.title: Dead weight
deadWeight.text: {part} only works on a lander. It flew for nothing.

noFavorite.title: Instruments don't fit the goal
noFavorite.text: None of your instruments is a specialist for this goal.

assembly.heading: Build the Spacecraft
assembly.allGood: All systems nominal. Ready for the launch window.

window.heading: Pick a Launch Date
window.mapLabel: Map of planet positions and transfer path
window.whereLater: where it will be when you arrive
window.legendMove: how far the planet moves during the trip

launch.maxQ: MAX Q: strongest air pressure on the rocket
launch.separation: First stage empty and dropped: a lighter rocket climbs faster
launch.inOrbit: In orbit at 7.8 km/s. Next stop: {destination}
launch.loading: Rolling the rocket out to the pad…
launch.ignitionCaption: The engines start a few seconds before lift-off, so the computer can check that they work.
launch.spaceCaption: Above about 100 km the air is almost gone and the sky turns black. This is space.
launch.boosterCaption: The boosters are empty and fall away. Less weight, more speed.
launch.fairingCaption: The nose cone opens. It protected the spacecraft from the air; in space it is only extra weight.
launch.craftCaption: Springs push the spacecraft away from the rocket. From now on it flies on its own.
launch.deploySolar: The solar panels unfold: the spacecraft now makes its own electricity.
launch.deployRtg: The RTG makes electricity from heat, so there are no panels to unfold.
launch.departCaption: The last push: about 11 km/s, fast enough to break free of Earth's pull. Next stop: {destination}.

mission.heading: {name} Mission in Progress
mission.timedFoot: No decision in time = {choice}. Not deciding is also a decision.

debrief.heading: Mission Report
debrief.summary: Worked {months} · {share}% of data reached Earth · {cost} spent
debrief.scienceExplain: How much of the goal's science reached Earth.
debrief.efficiencyExplain: Money left over and a rocket that fits the job.
debrief.decisionsExplain: How you handled problems during the flight.
